name: Wave2Net
customers_source: Not stated on website or BEAD letter
signals: Fixed wireless provider since 2003 that has begun deploying fiber-to-the-home (BEAD letter, Nov 2024)
Coverage page says to call 540-667-2672 to confirm availability; no online availability form seen
Coverage page says it 'can provide Internet Access throughout the United States with our partner networks'
Sells residential and business service
Advertises WaveOlution plan of up to 20 Mbps down / 3 Mbps up
Filed a BEAD letter of intent listing 11 counties/cities
fact_hook: Wave2Net calls itself the Shenandoah Valley's first WISP and has run fixed wireless out of 250 Airport Road in Winchester since 2003; in late 2024 owner Rudy Worrell told the state it is now building fiber-to-the-home too.
notes: counties_served is the list of counties in its BEAD letter of intent ('List of counties to be served'), not a verified current coverage map.

name: iWiSP LLC
customers_source: Not stated; BEAD letter says its fiber infrastructure can reach about 2,500 units (passings, not customers)
signals: Wireless broadband provider for about 15 years; added fiber-to-the-home in early 2020
Built 50+ miles of underground fiber in the Louisa County area, doing the work in-house
Planned BEAD applications for Berkeley/Livingston (Spotsylvania) and Mineral/Bumpass (Louisa)
Describes itself as a small local company
fact_hook: iWiSP has done all its own construction, laying 50+ miles of underground fiber around Louisa County since 2020 under a 'To the last foot' model, on top of about 15 years of wireless service in Spotsylvania, Louisa, Orange and Caroline.
notes: Website blocked automated access (Cloudflare), so details come from its Nov 2024 BEAD letter. Letter was signed by Amber M. Johnson, Project Manager; owner not named.

name: Piedmont Broadband
customers_source: Not stated; website says 100+ access points as of 2024
signals: Already offers Starlink installation ($250 standard) for customers who need a backup circuit or can't reach one of its access points
Says its equipment is line-of-sight based and 'the terrain out here doesn't always cooperate'

Sells hosted business phone service

leader.name: Richard Pate and Russell Pate
leader.title: Owners (bought the company in 2021, per Rappahannock News)

fact_hook: Piedmont Broadband has served the ridges and hollows of Rappahannock County since 2008, and its site already lists Starlink installation at $250 for homes that can't reach one of its 100+ access points.
notes: Strongest fit: already installs Starlink. Owner names come from a 2021 Rappahannock News report (seen via search snippet; article is paywalled); website says only that the company 'changed hands' in 2021.

name: Firefly Fiber Broadband (Central Virginia Electric Cooperative)
customers_source: fireflyva.com homepage: 'More than 50,000 homes and businesses across central Virginia' (an Aug 2026 release said 48,000+ connections)
signals: Has a 'Check Availability & Register' flow on its website
Sells business internet, phone and outdoor Wi-Fi
RISE Project (2021): 13 counties, 45,000+ locations, 5,000 miles of fiber, $330M, funded partly by VATI grants
Won about $79M in the Dec 2021 VATI round to reach 36,000+ unserved locations (NRECA)
Also the ISP for fiber built in Rappahannock Electric Cooperative territory
fact_hook: Firefly launched in 2018 as CVEC's fiber subsidiary and recently passed 50,000 connections; Consumer Reports ranked it third nationally among fiber providers.
notes: HQ shown as the Lovingston mailing address on its site; NRECA (2022) said Firefly is headquartered in Arrington, also in Nelson County. Larger than most entries here.

name: B2X Online, Inc.
customers_source: Not stated; website says it serves 12 counties

fact_hook: B2X opened in June 2003 at 30 Mill Lane in Salem, where it still is today; the founders trained in Chicago on Motorola Canopy gear, and the company is still owned and run by the two founding brothers.
notes: counties_served lists its 'major service areas'; site says it reaches 12 counties in total. CEO name comes from a 2021 WDBJ article reposted on its site.

notes: Website says founded 2018 but its BEAD letter says 'over ten years'. Site lists 'Surry County, VA'; given the Cana location and 336 phone number this may mean Surry County, NC. Customer counts differ (400 vs 600+).

notes: BEAD letter lists both Rich Creek, VA (PO Box) and Bluefield, WV addresses.

fact_hook: Citizens traces its roots to 1914 in Floyd County, and in 2024 it finished a 707-mile fiber build that gave 100% of Floyd County residents access to 1 Gbps internet.
notes: counties_served lists only counties named on its site (Floyd plus cable systems in Carroll, Wythe, Craig, and Patrick/Meadows of Dan); site says 12 counties total but does not list them all.

Mountainous terrain in service area

notes: Website does not list counties; Giles County comes from its Pembroke location and USDA grant records.

Mountainous terrain in service area

fact_hook: SCTC took shape in late summer 1951 to bring phone service to 420 square miles of Scott County and 15 square miles of Hancock County, Tennessee, and its 2010 Broadband Incentive Program brought internet to 500+ square miles of the region.

name: Bee Online Advantage (Craig-Botetourt Electric Cooperative)
customers_source: Not stated
signals: Website has an availability check ('See if Bee Online Advantage is available in your area')

fact_hook: With about 7,000 meters, Craig-Botetourt was the smallest co-op to win a grant in Virginia's December 2021 broadband round, using about $1.6M to reach 495 unserved locations.
notes: Electric service covers seven counties; broadband says it is available in Alleghany, Botetourt and Roanoke counties.

customers_source: Not stated
